final_writeup:
This does not resolve the unrestricted target, but it gives exact reductions and rules out several substantial classes.

For a basis vector define P_ki=v_ki v_ki* and Q_ki=P_ki−I/6. In the real Hilbert space H0 of traceless Hermitian 6×6 matrices,
Tr(Q_ki Q_kj)=δ_ij−1/6, and Tr(Q_ki Q_lj)=0 for k≠l.
Thus D_k=span{Q_ki} has dimension 5, and seven MUBs are exactly an orthogonal decomposition H0=D_1⊕⋯⊕D_7 into traceless diagonal subspaces. In particular, for any six MUBs their orthogonal complement W has dimension 5, and they extend to seven if and only if all elements of W commute. Indeed, an extension gives W=D_7; conversely, commuting Hermitian matrices are simultaneously diagonalizable, and dimension 5 forces W to be the entire traceless diagonal space of the resulting basis. This also makes the extension unique.

The simplex frame identity inside each D_k implies, for a complete set and every matrix A,
Σ_ki Tr(AP_ki)P_ki=A+Tr(A)I.
Equivalently, with F the tensor flip,
Σ_ki P_ki⊗P_ki=I+F.
Consequently every unit x satisfies Σ_ki |⟨x,v_ki⟩|^4=2. If x is unbiased to any six of the bases, those bases contribute 1, so the six probabilities in the remaining basis have sum and squared sum both 1. Hence x is exactly one of that basis's rays. Thus any six bases have at most one completion, and under a completion their common-unbiased locus has exactly six rays.

Now identify C^6=C^2⊗C^3. For ρ_A=Tr_B(P_ki), the swap identity and the tensor moment give
Σ_ki Tr(ρ_A^2)=Tr[(I+F_A⊗F_B)(F_A⊗I)]=2·3^2+2^2·3=30.
Every such purity lies in [1/2,1], with value 1 precisely for a product vector and 1/2 precisely for a maximally entangled vector. If P of the 42 rays are product, then 30≥P+(42−P)/2, so P≤18. Hence at most three bases can consist entirely of product vectors; if three do, all remaining 24 vectors must be maximally entangled.

This can be sharpened for direct tensor-product bases. Any three MUBs in C^3 extend uniquely to four. To see this from scratch, fix the first two as the standard and Fourier bases. With ω=e^(2πi/3), every ray unbiased to both is
x_pq=(1,ω^p,ω^q)/√3
for one of
(0,1),(0,2),(1,0),(1,1),(2,0),(2,2).
The orthogonal triples are exactly {(0,1),(1,0),(2,2)} and {(0,2),(1,1),(2,0)}, and the two triples are mutually unbiased. The reduction to this list follows from the cyclic-autocorrelation equation a+conj(a)b+conj(b)=0: its three unit-modulus terms have product 1 and sum 0, so they are the three cube roots of unity.

Suppose A_k⊗B_k, k=1,2,3, are direct-product MUBs. Their local factors are pairwise MUBs. No maximally entangled ψ can be unbiased to all three. Indeed, write its qutrit reduced state as Π_S/2, with S two-dimensional. Uniform product probabilities imply that the ray w=S-perp is unbiased to B_1,B_2,B_3, hence w belongs to their unique fourth basis B_4. Let c_0,c_1 be the other B_4 vectors and write ψ=(a_0⊗c_0+a_1⊗c_1)/√2. Conditional qubit states obtained from every b∈B_k are unbiased to the same basis {a_0,a_1}. For each k these three conditional rays form a unit-norm tight frame in C^2, so this is the unique qubit basis unbiased to all three rays. Uniformity would therefore force A_1=A_2=A_3, contradicting their mutual unbiasedness. Combining this with the purity budget proves that no complete seven-MUB set can contain three direct tensor-product bases; it can contain at most two.

There are also exact arithmetic obstructions to two common finite constructions. If, after making one basis standard, all remaining coordinates are sixth roots ζ^r/√6, the inner product of vectors from two nonstandard bases would require |S|^2=6 for a sum S of six sixth roots. Writing S=A+Bζ gives |S|^2=A^2+AB+B^2. Equality to 6 is impossible: modulo 2 it forces A,B even, after which the norm is divisible by 4. The same conclusion holds for fourth-root phases because A^2+B^2=6 is impossible modulo 3. Thus either phase alphabet permits at most the standard basis plus one other basis.

Finally, the standard Weyl–Heisenberg stabilizer construction in dimension 6 yields at most three MUBs. Its bases correspond to order-six isotropic subgroups L≤Z_6^2; two resulting bases are unbiased exactly when their subgroups intersect only at zero. Every order-six subgroup contains a nonzero involution, while Z_6^2 has only three nonzero involutions: (3,0),(0,3),(3,3). Hence at most three such subgroups can be pairwise disjoint. The bound is attained by the horizontal, vertical, and diagonal cyclic subgroups.

The remaining unrestricted case would require an orthogonal decomposition into seven diagonal subspaces with at most two direct-product bases, unrestricted phases, and no Weyl stabilizer structure; none of the arguments above excludes that core case.

results.claim: For pairwise MUBs, their centered rank-one projectors span mutually orthogonal five-dimensional traceless diagonal subspaces; seven MUBs are equivalent to an orthogonal decomposition of the 35-dimensional traceless Hermitian space into seven such subspaces.
results.proof_sketch: Let P_ki=v_ki v_ki* and Q_ki=P_ki−I/6. Directly from the MUB identities, Tr(Q_ki Q_kj)=δ_ij−1/6, while Tr(Q_ki Q_lj)=0 for k≠l. The within-basis Gram matrix is I_6−J_6/6, of rank 5. Thus every basis supplies a five-dimensional subspace D_k, and distinct D_k are orthogonal. Seven of them have total dimension 7·5=35, exactly the dimension of traceless Hermitian 6×6 matrices. Conversely, orthogonality of two such centered diagonal spaces gives Tr(P_kiP_lj)=1/6, hence mutual unbiasedness.

results.claim: Given any six MUBs in C^6, let W be the orthogonal complement of their six centered diagonal subspaces. They extend to a seventh MUB if and only if every pair of matrices in W commutes; if so, the extension is unique.
results.proof_sketch: The six subspaces have total dimension 30, so dim W=5. If a seventh basis exists, its centered diagonal subspace is contained in W and also has dimension 5, hence equals W and is commuting. Conversely, if W consists of commuting Hermitian matrices, simultaneous diagonalization embeds it into the five-dimensional space of traceless diagonal matrices in some basis. Equality of dimensions makes it that entire space. Its common eigenbasis is unbiased to the original six by orthogonality of centered projectors. The full diagonal algebra has one-dimensional joint eigenspaces, so it determines that basis up to phases and permutation.

results.claim: A complete set of seven MUBs satisfies the reconstruction identity Σ_ki Tr(AP_ki)P_ki=A+Tr(A)I and the tensor identity Σ_ki P_ki⊗P_ki=I+F.
results.proof_sketch: For each k, the simplex {Q_ki} has frame operator equal to the identity on D_k. Since the seven D_k orthogonally fill the traceless Hermitian space, Σ_ki Tr(AQ_ki)Q_ki=A for traceless A. The scalar part and Σ_ki P_ki=7I then give Σ Tr(AP_ki)P_ki=A+Tr(A)I for arbitrary A. Testing its two sides against product matrices A⊗B yields Σ Tr(AP_ki)Tr(BP_ki)=Tr(AB)+Tr(A)Tr(B), which is exactly the pairing with I+F; product matrices span the full tensor matrix space.

results.claim: In a complete set, every unit vector x obeys Σ_ki |⟨x,v_ki⟩|^4=2; a vector unbiased to any chosen six bases must be a ray of the remaining basis.
results.proof_sketch: Apply the reconstruction identity to P_x=xx* and take its Hilbert–Schmidt inner product with P_x. This gives the fourth-power sum 2. Six unbiased bases contribute 36·(1/6)^2=1. If p_i are the measurement probabilities in the remaining basis, then Σp_i=1 and Σp_i^2=1. Nonnegative probabilities have this property only when one equals 1 and the rest vanish, so x is one of the remaining basis vectors.

results.claim: For any hypothetical complete set and any fixed identification C^6=C^2⊗C^3, the sum of the 42 qubit reduced purities is exactly 30.
results.proof_sketch: For P=|v⟩⟨v|, the swap identity gives Tr[(Tr_B P)^2]=Tr[P⊗P(F_A⊗I_BB)]. Sum over the complete set and substitute ΣP⊗P=I+F_A⊗F_B. The trace is Tr(F_A)Tr(I_BB)+Tr(I_AA)Tr(F_B)=2·9+4·3=30.

results.claim: Relative to any fixed C^2⊗C^3 factorization, a complete set contains at most 18 product rays and at most three entirely product bases. Equality forces every other ray to be maximally entangled.
results.proof_sketch: A qubit reduced density matrix of a bipartite pure state has purity at least 1/2. Its purity is 1 exactly for a product state, and equality at the lower bound means eigenvalues 1/2,1/2, i.e. maximal entanglement. If P rays are product, the total purity is at least P+(42−P)/2=21+P/2. Since it equals 30, P≤18. Three product bases already contribute 18 product rays, so equality holds and every remaining contribution must be 1/2.

results.claim: For any fixed conjugation K, a complete set has at most 12 K-real rays and hence at most two bases consisting entirely of K-real rays.
results.proof_sketch: In coordinates where K is entrywise conjugation, let Ω=Σ_r e_r⊗e_r. For a unit v, ⟨Ω|P_v⊗P_v|Ω⟩=|Σ_r v_r^2|^2. Summing and using I+F gives 2∥Ω∥^2=12. A ray is fixed by K precisely when this nonnegative statistic equals 1. Thus there can be at most 12 such rays. If 12 occur, every remaining ray satisfies Σ_r v_r^2=0.

results.claim: Two direct tensor-product bases in C^2⊗C^3 are mutually unbiased if and only if their respective qubit bases and qutrit bases are mutually unbiased.
results.proof_sketch: The forward implication follows by writing squared product overlaps as α_rsβ_tu=1/6. Fixing t,u makes every α_rs equal; row normalization in dimension 2 forces α_rs=1/2, and then β_tu=1/3. The converse is immediate by multiplying local overlap magnitudes. Hence three direct-product MUBs yield triples of local MUBs.

results.claim: Every triple of MUBs in C^3 extends uniquely to four MUBs, and the rays unbiased to all three are exactly the fourth basis.
results.proof_sketch: Send the first basis to the standard basis. Every 3×3 complex Hadamard matrix is equivalent to the Fourier matrix: after dephasing, a row orthogonal to (1,1,1) must contain 1,ω,ω². A standard-flat ray is x_pq=(1,ω^p,ω^q)/√3. Fourier-unbiasedness is equivalent to ω^p+ω^(q−p)+ω^(−q)=0. The three summands have modulus one and product one, so they must be 1,ω,ω² in some order. This gives exactly six pairs: (0,1),(0,2),(1,0),(1,1),(2,0),(2,2). Their only orthogonal triples are {(0,1),(1,0),(2,2)} and {(0,2),(1,1),(2,0)}; direct substitution shows the two triples are mutually unbiased. A third basis must be one triple, leaving the other as the unique fourth and exact common-unbiased locus.

results.claim: If three unit qubit rays form a tight frame with frame operator 3I/2 and are all unbiased to one qubit basis, that basis is the unique qubit basis unbiased to all three rays.
results.proof_sketch: Their centered projectors lie in the two-dimensional real plane of traceless Hermitian matrices with zero diagonal in the given basis, and their sum is zero. They cannot span only a line: equal projector norms would make each one ±Q, and three signs cannot sum to zero. They therefore span the whole plane. The traceless diagonal observable of any basis unbiased to all three rays must be orthogonal to this plane, whose orthogonal complement is the single line determined by the original basis.

results.claim: No maximally entangled vector in C^2⊗C^3 is unbiased to three pairwise MUB direct tensor-product bases.
results.proof_sketch: Write the bases as A_k⊗B_k. For maximally entangled ψ, its qutrit reduction is Π_S/2. If ψ is unbiased to all three product bases, summing over the two qubit outcomes shows ⟨b|Π_S|b⟩=2/3 for every b∈B_k. Thus the ray w=S-perp is unbiased to B_1,B_2,B_3 and, by the qutrit classification, belongs to their fourth basis B_4. Let c_0,c_1 be the other B_4 rays. Maximal entanglement permits ψ=(a_0⊗c_0+a_1⊗c_1)/√2. Since every B_k is unbiased to B_4, every normalized conditional qubit state obtained from b∈B_k is unbiased to the same basis {a_0,a_1}. For fixed k the three conditional states have frame operator 3I/2. Uniform product probabilities also make them unbiased to A_k. The preceding qubit lemma forces every A_k to equal {a_0,a_1}, contradicting pairwise mutual unbiasedness.

results.claim: A complete seven-MUB set in C^2⊗C^3 cannot contain three direct tensor-product bases; consequently it contains at most two such bases.
results.proof_sketch: Three direct-product bases contribute 18 product rays. The purity bound then forces every vector in the other four bases to be maximally entangled. Each such vector would have to be unbiased to all three product bases, contradicting the preceding maximally-entangled-vector obstruction.

results.claim: If one basis is standard and every vector in every other basis has coordinates consisting entirely of fourth roots, or entirely of sixth roots, divided by √6, then the MUB family has at most two bases.
results.proof_sketch: For two nonstandard sixth-root-flat vectors, unbiasedness requires |S|^2=6, where S is a sum of six sixth roots. With ζ=e^(πi/3), write S=A+Bζ; then |S|^2=A^2+AB+B^2. Modulo 2, an even value forces A and B even, making the norm divisible by 4, not 6. For fourth roots, S=A+iB and A^2+B^2=6. Reduction modulo 3 forces A,B divisible by 3, also impossible. Thus no vectors from two distinct nonstandard bases can be mutually unbiased.

results.claim: For the standard dimension-six Weyl construction, order-six isotropic subgroups L≤Z_6^2 give stabilizer bases, and two such bases are mutually unbiased exactly when their label subgroups intersect only at zero.
results.proof_sketch: For X and Z the shift and phase operators, the 36 Weyl matrices X^aZ^b are Hilbert–Schmidt orthogonal. An isotropic order-six subgroup L gives a commuting six-dimensional star-algebra, hence a maximal diagonal algebra and a rank-one joint eigenbasis. Its traceless part is spanned by the five nonidentity Weyl labels in L. Two such traceless algebras are orthogonal exactly when their nonzero label sets are disjoint; orthogonality of centered rank-one projectors is equivalent to mutual unbiasedness.

results.claim: At most three pairwise MUB stabilizer bases arise from the dimension-six Weyl construction, and three are attainable.
results.proof_sketch: Every order-six subgroup contains a nonzero element u with 2u=0: pair elements with their negatives, noting that the five nonzero elements cannot all form two-element pairs. The only nonzero 2-torsion labels in Z_6^2 are (3,0),(0,3),(3,3). Pairwise-trivially-intersecting subgroups must use distinct such labels, so there are at most three. The cyclic subgroups {(t,0)}, {(0,t)}, and {(t,t)} are order six, isotropic, and pairwise intersect only at zero, attaining the bound.
